meta.source: NSE corporate-share-holdings-master -> the SEBI shareholding-pattern XBRL instance per filing (nsearchives). Official filings, not a scrape.
meta.grain: one row per (symbol, quarter end, named shareholder)

definitions.pct: the holder's stake as a percentage of total shares, as filed. The source stores a FRACTION (0.0688 = 6.88%); it is scaled to percent once, at parse.
definitions.d_pp: change in that holder's percentage vs the SAME stock's previous filed quarter, in percentage POINTS. Not a rupee flow.
definitions.action: new / exit / add / trim / hold on a 0.05pp threshold; 'unknown' when the stock has only one filed quarter, so no comparison exists.
definitions.fpi_named_pct: sum of the NAMED foreign holders' percentages for that stock — a FLOOR on foreign ownership, not the total (see the caveats).
definitions.holders: the reverse index: one foreign investor and every Indian position it discloses. This is the 13F-equivalent view.

caveats: ONLY holders above 1% must be named, so this is a FLOOR on foreign ownership and is systematically thin for mega-caps whose FPI money is spread over many sub-1% funds. Measured 2026-06: RELIANCE names ZERO foreign holders, HDFCBANK 4, while small/mid caps name 7-11. Do not read a low count as low foreign interest.

Quarterly and lagged — filings land over several weeks, so the newest quarter is only partly filed. Change is computed per stock on ITS own two most recent filed quarters and both dates ride on every row.
Holder identity is a normalised NAME, not a registry id. Distinct funds of one manager may or may not consolidate depending on how the filer wrote the name.
holder_type comes from the category the FILER chose in the XBRL, so a fund mis-categorised at source is mis-typed here too.
Percentages are of each company's own share count — they are not rupee amounts and must never be summed across stocks as if they were.
